title: Eye Highlights, Tool Groups, and Crop Tricks: Photoshop Tools for Beginners (Lesson 2)
summary: This beginner-focused Photoshop lesson teaches practical, repeatable techniques for reinforcing non-destructive editing and core tool navigation. It starts with a quick, hands-on eye-light enhancement using a soft round brush on a new layer and an Overlay blend mode to create bright catch lights. The instructor then dissects the Photoshop toolbar into tool groups, demonstrates non-destructive workflows (new layers, sampling across layers, and tool settings via the Options bar), and walks through patching and removing on separate layers. The session continues with toolbar customization (editing, hiding, and saving presets such as Pix Minimal), followed by foundational cropping basics, including delete-cropped-pixels caution, fixed vs freehand ratios, and the straightening workflow with a reference point that can be moved with Alt/Option. The video also covers Generative Expand (AI-assisted content-aware expansion), model prompts, and option handling, plus Move tool behavior, alignment options (align to selection vs align to canvas), and a hybrid approach for temporarily enabling Auto Select with a Ctrl/Cmd modifier. Throughout, the educator emphasizes practical shortcuts, workflow hygiene, and practicing on a separate layer to stay non-destructive, ending with encouragement to follow along and apply these tools to own projects.

sections.title: Kickstart Tools - A Fun Project
sections.description: A quick, guided exercise using a soft round brush on a new layer to add light to the eyes. The presenter emphasizes checking the catch light, choosing a soft brush, and then changing the layer blend mode to Overlay for a natural glow. The example includes swapping foreground/background colors, resizing the brush with bracket keys, and erasing extras with a tilde-enabled brush. Opacity on the layer is adjustable to tone the effect.
